summary: Christian Bernert is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Mag. phil. at the University of Vienna under MA supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes, also studying under Junjie Chu, Karin Preisendanz, and Gerald Hödl, and attended the International Buddhist Academy.

Christian Coseru works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the Australian National University (~1999–2003) under John Powers, having also studied under Sibajiban Bhattacharyya. His career includes fellowships at the Asiatic Society and an associate professorship at the College of Charleston (~2006).

Christian Gottlob Heyne was an 18th-century scholar of linguistics and history and archaeology. After studying at Leipzig University (~1748–1752), he held a post at the University of Göttingen from around 1763 to 1812, teaching August Wilhelm Schlegel and Johann Gottfried Eichhorn.

Christian Haskett specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2010), having also studied under Robert A. F. Thurman, Michael Chamberlain, Lobsang Jamspal, and L. Gyaltsen, and held a post at Washington and Lee University (attested 2010).

Christian K. Wedemeyer works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Wesleyan University and Columbia University (PhD ~1993–1999 under Robert A. F. Thurman), and held posts at the University of Copenhagen (~2000–2003) and the University of Chicago (Professor ~2003).

Christian Karl Josias von Bunsen was a scholar in linguistics, religious studies, and history and archaeology. He pursued his education at the University of Marburg (~1808–1809) and the University of Göttingen (~1809–1812).

Christian Lassen was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Heidelberg University and the University of Bonn, where he learned from August Wilhelm Schlegel. Lassen served as extraordinary professor (1830) and professor of Old Indian Language and Literature (1840–1876) at Bonn.

Christian Lee Novetzke specializes in Indology, religious studies, and history and archaeology. Educated at Macalester College, Harvard University, Harvard Divinity School, and Columbia University, he taught at the University of Pennsylvania (~2002–2008) before becoming a professor at the University of Washington (~2008).

Christian Lindtner was a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies who completed his doktorgrad at the University of Copenhagen by 1982. He served as a professor at the University of Copenhagen between at least 1980 and 1991.

Christian Luczanits works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and history and archaeology. After completing his Magister and PhD (-1998) at the University of Vienna, he held posts at Vienna, Stanford, UC Berkeley, Lumbini International Research Institute, and the Rubin Museum of Art (curator, 2012).

Christian Matthias Boehm is a scholar of Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of John T. Carpenter (attested 2005).

Christian Wittern specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He held an attested professorship and posts at Kyoto University (attested 1993, 2008) and was affiliated with Hanazono University (attested 2011).
Christine Chojnacki is an Indologist who completed her doctoral thesis at Sorbonne Nouvelle University in 1991. She served as a professor at Jean Moulin University Lyon 3 (attested 2018).

Christine Mollier is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied under Kristofer Schipper. She served at CNRS as a researcher (1989–1995) and Research Director (attested 2006–2014), and was a visiting professor at the University of Chicago.

Christoph Anderl is a scholar in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He earned his MA at the University of Vienna (-1995) and completed his PhD at the University of Oslo (~1997–2002) under Christoph Harbsmeier.

Christoph Cüppers is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Hamburg (~1974–1983) under Lambert Schmithausen, Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan, and Albrecht Wezler, later serving as Director of the Lumbini International Research Institute (~1993–2013).

Christoph Emmrich specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Heidelberg University (PhD 2004), where he also held a post attested in 2001, and later became an assistant professor at the University of Toronto.

Christoph Harbsmeier is a scholar in Sinology and linguistics who studied at the University of Oxford and earned his PhD from the University of Copenhagen. He was a professor at the University of Oslo (~1985–2014) and held advisory professorships in China (2001).

Christoph Kleine is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who completed his PhD and Habilitation at the University of Marburg. He was a professor at LMU Munich (2004–2008) and Leipzig University (~2008), with research at EFEO.

Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf was a scholar of history and archaeology and Indology. He served as Chair of Asian Anthropology at the University of London (~1951–1976) and was a professor at SOAS University of London (attested 1988).
